\textit{Note:} 21 OECD members before 2000: those with informal employment below 25\% of employment (left out: Korea, Mexico, Turkey) where one public pay-as-you-go system pays the bulk of retirement benefits, that is, funded tiers pay less than a quarter of mandatory benefits in 2020 and the public pension is not tested against them (left out: Australia, Denmark, Iceland, Netherlands, Switzerland). The Bismarckian index is $I = 1/(2-\theta)$, with $\theta$ the least-squares slope of the public pension on earnings at 0.5, 1 and 2 times average earnings (Pensions at a Glance 2021) times one minus the share of spending on minimum top-ups and tested benefits. Pension spending is public cash spending on old age and survivors, 2020, in \% of GDP; population growth is the population of 2020 over that of 1990; the Gini is that of disposable income.
